newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Central America wants a U.S. amnesty for immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Central America wants a U.S. amnesty for immigrants.

text.p: Salvadoran President Armando Calderon said on Monday that Central American leaders planned to ask U.S. President Bill Clinton for an amnesty for millions of illegal immigrants.
Millions of Central American illegal immigrants live in the United States and are subject to a new U.S. immigration law that curtails their rights and makes them easier targets for deportation.
Clinton and regional leaders are scheduled to meet in Costa Rica on Wednesday. The summit marks Clinton's first trip to the region as president.
"We will ask for an amnesty, and I believe this is the least that the presidents of Central America and myself can ask for," Calderon said at a news conference.
Calderon denounced the "witch hunt" he claimed has started in various cities in the United States since the new immigration law came into force this year.

More than one million Salvadorans live in cities in the United States, and they form an important support for the economy in the poor Central American nation, sending more than $1 billion home each year, he said.

Calderon said the immigration issue along with free trade will be examined by Clinton and the president of Costa Rica, Jose Maria Figueres, of Nicaragua, Arnoldo Aleman, of Honduras, Carlos Reina and of Guatemala, Alvaro Arzu.
"We are closely tied, since while the chance of improving one's standard of living don't exist here, there was always the chance of migrating to the United States," he said.
"If the United States does not want more immigrants we have to think that this region will have to make a leap in the quality of development and only by this will flows of migrants stop," he said.

The Central American nations will also present Clinton with the idea of negotiating a free trade agreement and hope that a commission to analyse the idea will be one result of the meeting. "We are not asking for aid, we are asking for trade, for investment, to be true business partners for development," he said.
